item.title: 08 Nov 2026 10:30
item.description:
ASKY is one of the more reliable airlines in West Africa. They however keep shifting their flight schedules quite frequently. During our last trip to Malabo they altered the schedule last minute and we had to fly all the way down to Addis to get back to Yaounde. During both our onward and return flights this time we had to fly via Lome. Travel to constituents is such a pain here in Africa at times.

Just got back from a short walk in and around Parque Nacional. This is just a couple minutes from the hotel and is actually quite a well maintained park. Nothing in Yaounde comes close to this, so I’m glad we did get out this Sunday morning. The heat’s real but nothing too much to handle.

It’s highly likely we might know where we’re headed next year by end of this week. Exciting! Just really hope it’s one of those places with easy access to the outdoors.

It’s Diwali today! And one like none other. I should really plan and block these days on my calendar. Would have been real nice just being at home today. I’d like to eat something wicked delicious. One of those lip-smacking Biryani’s? or Maybe a real well done Mysore Masasla Dosa and Sambhar from that Krishna Udipi Bhawan in Vidyanagar. For today though, I’ll have to settle in for a pizza slice that’s microwave heated well beyond it’s heat-point and served on a plastic plate….

Spent some time tweaking this site to reflect a few things I’ve had in my mind. Ever since I started the model rail project, I’ve spent way little time here. Every hobby gives and takes I guess! 🔗

item.title: 24 Oct 2026 10:30
item.description:
We finally made it to Ebogo this morning! Been on our list for a while now but for some reason it never materialized. About 55 kms from home with the last 7 kms through unpaved road - Getting there was super straight forward.

Alexis our guide greeted us cheerfully and quickly got us into the Padauk pirogues. Skirting the corners, he moved us upstream steadily for about 90 minutes.

With abundant monsoon this season, River Nyong was at about 26ft apparently. Summer is right round the corner and he doesn’t anticipate it reaching it’s peak average depth of 40ft.

Parts of the forest were submerged and he took us into the woods. Weaving into and out of these trees was pretty awesome! You could feel a sudden drop in temperature here.

As we made our way out of the forest and back into main river, Alexis mentioned he’d seen a documentary about the dowry system in India and that he kept telling his wife he should have gotten married there instead. The groom pays the bride’s family in this part of the world!

Once out of the woods, Alexis steered us across the river towards the northwest and for a quick shore stop at Kossipo. The magnificent Kossipo tree believed to be ~1200 years old spans about 25-30ft in diameter and punches up to about 280ft high! We got some quick bites from those large black ants on the way up to the tree. On the way back S&I made sure we ran as quickly as we could.

The return leg from Kossipo was all downstream and we probably got back in about 25 minutes. Grabbed a decent bite at the restaurant and made our way back to Yaounde. I think our GV would have made it in and out but I am glad we got out right before it started raining. Wouldn’t be fun to be stuck in muck! Return was super straight forward following the Organic Maps’ directions. Google maps seems to have taken us through the inner roads for no reason earlier this morning.

Alexis promised he’d let us actually handle the oars if we let him know before hand. So maybe one more trip is due here. Otherwise this was a pretty quick and nice getaway! 🔗

item.title: 02 Oct 2026 10:30
item.description:
One of the perks of my job is to meet and work with so many interesting people. And with anything that awesome, it’s almost always short-lived. People move on once their assignment comes to an end and somebody else comes and fills their shoes. Snyder is leaving us this weekend and he will very much be missed!

We have an unsaid practice in ST to host Thirsty Thursday’s. It’s a HUGE morale booster for a bunch of teams and turns out to be great way to get folks together just before the week comes to an end. Snyder was a frequent TT participant and we’ll absolutely miss him.

Made him a miniature representation of TT last night. Took me around 4 hours to get it to this state and I think I’m going to leave this as is and not color it. Coloring is not my artsy forte yet and I think this kinda gives him (or his grandkids) a platform to build-on. Until next, Snyder! 1600 somewhere on TTs. 🔗

item.title: 27 Sep 2026 10:30
item.description:
Over the last few weeks, I’ve been contemplating how exactly I would like to set this Model rail diorama. My primary concern was mobility. I want to be able to dismantle it quickly if needed and pack these all up into two or three big boxes. Ideally I would stage this on a wooden platform, staged on a wall at shoulder height. Wasn’t quite lucky finding the wood I would need for that and then given we only have about 10 months left here, I wasn’t invested enough.

Yesterday morning, It struck me to use the surfboard’s box as a platform. Staged it on the ground in our master bedroom and quickly threw a bedsheet on top of it. Added 6 25cents coins on each compartments underside for stability weight and tested out the connections. The engine rides beautifully, but the compartments still detach randomly. Decided to troubleshoot that later - Will most likely have to add a couple more coins and check the couplers later..

While at it, I reworked the rail platform a bit. I’d previously built a platform using paper mache. That didn’t feel strong enough and was warping a bit. Built another platform using balsa wood and that turned out pretty good. Need to add more stabilizers later. Eventually I want to add more responsive lighting in. Built some tiny benches and then tiny people. I think they’ve turned out pretty neat! Still need to figure out the colors et al. But I think I’ve learnt how to work the wood and the tiny people was a fantastic add-on I’m super proud of!

Here’s what I’ve visualized this whole setup to look like: The rail-line would meander around a large water body via a couple tunnels to make it’s way to the platform. Each side of the platform would have rail lines - ideally with switchover connections. The platform would connect to the station via an overhead walkover bridge. The land around the station and by the rails would all be decked by miniature features you’d find in the country-side. Would be wonderful to add a waterfall, some clouds (that move?) and some neat visual effects.

Each of these tiny miniatures takes several hours and multiple takes. This is turning out to be way more involved than I had imagined, but I’m absolutely loving it. Been a while that something has gotten my attention so much! 🔗

item.title: 11 Sep 2026 10:30
item.description:
The marines organized a stair climb event this morning to commemorate 9/11. Climbed 3 floors 38 times. They had their flaks on and one of them even had a gas mask on. I was breathing hard at the end of the 10th lap. Legs felt quite jelly by the 20th. Started sipping water from the 25th lap and finally finished reasonably good at the 38th. A good cold shower was all that was needed to feel normal. Oddly this felt a bit more challenging than last time.

I was around 15 when we got the news of the twin towers. Miss Bama was supposed to be landing in the U.S that day. We’d only hear a day later that her flight was routed to Canada and someone drove her over to where she had to get to.

25 years have passed and we’re still at it! Paying the 911 tax - $5.60 for every single flight ticket that you take on U.S soil. Any perceived victory in any war is all just a mirage. 🔗

item.title: 23 Aug 2026 10:30
item.description:
It’s here! This is an absolute piece of beauty and I can already imagine how this could be a wicked good hobby! So many ideas on how I want to stage this! This whole kit came decently packed but I did have to super-glue some components that had popped off or broken during transit. The WAP5 kit has the WAP5 Engine, 3 LHB Rajdhani coaches and an 18 inch radius oval track. For now, I’ve staged all of these scaled models in an infento case and over the next several days, I plan to design a modular and portable diorama so I can easily dismantle and store them. The engine zooms on these tracks and barely derails. The coaches on the other hand seem to be extremely sensitive to non-straight tracks. Quite likely because they’re so light [ ~100 gms]! I need to make sure when I set these rails in a diorama, I tether them to the base and then maybe add some extra load to make the coaches glide on the rails.

As I’m trying to imagine what I’d like this setup to look like here’s what I currently have in mind.

  • A long straight stretch ~ 12 ft long at the minimum and has space to hold atleast two HO tracks in parallel. This should give me enough distance to place a couple stations, some hill inclines and maybe a bridge? Ideally, I would like this to be built so I can add more blocks in between as my imagination evolves.
  • A corner block that let’s me build a proper rail junction. This would be the staging area for locomotives that aren’t actively running.

Fun upgrades:

  • Add realistic sound programming! That would be terrific!
  • Proper lighting at the rail level where the engine and locomotives are being staged.
  • An optimized switch system. The current switch control is bulky and non intuitive.
  • Sensor based tracks. The engine should stop when it senses an end of track. 🔗

item.title: 20 Jul 2026 10:30
item.description:
Amidst all this travel, I finally got some time to install GrapheneOS on the refurbished Pixel 8 Pro that I bought last month. Boy, that was the easiest OS install I’ve done in a while. Barely took my 10 minutes from start to finish. And having spent a few weeks with GrapheneOS as my primary driver. It’s nothing short of amazing!

I love that it’s so vanilla! My main profile has apps mostly installed via Obtainium and F-Droid. For the needy apps, I installed a user profile specifically with Play Store and services. This profile is mostly turned off. And I love that each app is sandboxed by default!

Should have made this transition way before! I don’t quite need all the ‘privacy’ features that GrapheneOS touts but it’s remarkable that they’ve made it so freaking simple for anybody to install this on their phones. 🔗

item.title: 13 Jun 2026 10:30
item.description:
Rishi’s most recent newsletter sent me down a rabbit-hole on the Palakkad Gap - the lowest and most significant mountain pass in the Western Ghats in India. It all makes sense now - The weather patterns, our ancestral migration, the language effect…

And then the word Kerala was derived from Cheralam. The Cheras Dynasty ruled this part of India then and the Palakkad Gap was instrumental in the Chola Dynasty engaging with the Cheras. Malayalam evolved from a western dialect of Old Tamil and was heavily influenced by Sanskrit. The words Pattar and Bhat evolved from sanskrit word bhaṭṭa! And the word Malayalam is most likely derived from mala and alam - language of the mountainous region.

This is all so fascinating! 🔗
